FSAM program will put some much needed cash into the hands of Canadian farmers before spring seeding.
Together, FSAM I and II will make available $1.4 billion in federal transitional assistance until the GRIP and NISA programs fully kick in.
The bulk of the recently announced money will go to grains and oilseeds producers. They will receive $700 million, paid out in two instalments with the first going out within a month or so. The remaining $100 million will be shared by the horticulture producers, the maple syrup industry, mink and fox fur ranchers and honey producers.
The government continues to support Canadian farmers as it has in the past. Since 1983, and we have said this many times, government spending on agriculture has increased by 650 per cent. In 1986 this government provided farmers with $1 billion under the special grains program. In 1987 another $1.1 billion was made available under the same program and there was another $850 million under the drought assistance program and $500 million under the special income assistance program for
1990.
The Government of Canada has demonstrated by both word and deed that it is prepared to stand by farmers during this difficult time. We understand their situation and we are responding.
We could go on and talk at length about this, but we are committed to the future of agriculture in this country. We have stood by farmers in the most difficult times. We will be there when they need us and we will be there for the future.

Mr. Speaker, in the minister's response to my oral question of October 31, 1991, he made reference to refugee camps and internment, planting the innuendo that either I or my party advocate what his junior minister, the member for Rimouski-Temiscouata, has characterized as concentration camps.
This innuendo arose out of an article which appeared in The Ottawa Citizen on October 24, 1991. The story later appeared in one form or another in many newspapers in the Southam chain.
The story referred to a proposal for refugee work camps which were stated to be a part of an immigration discussion paper which I had written.
The impression is false, because the minister relied not on the facts but on the article. It has thereby cast aspersions on me and my party. Because others across the country have jumped to false conclusions based on a distorted article, I want to set the record straight.
The leader of my party requested that I prepare a paper on immigration. Its purpose was to generate discussion about all aspects of immigration in order for us in the Liberal Party to work toward a just and compassionate immigration policy for the nineties and beyond.
I did as I was requested. My preliminary paper is 71 pages long and contains over 30 recommendations for discussion. I submitted my paper to the appropriate caucus committee in accordance with established party procedure. Thus out of 81 of my colleagues I gave the paper to only 9. To this date I have not given a copy to any other person in my caucus. Why? Because as immigration critic I am voluntarily bound by the rules and procedures Liberals have adopted for the examination and debate of discussion papers. My paper is still at the preliminary discussion stage at the appropriate committee level.
My paper was leaked by a person or persons as yet unknown to The Ottawa Citizen. It was then again leaked later to both the Toronto Star and Maclean's magazine. The reported stories grossly distort the few recommendations talked about and use inflammatory words not found anywhere in my paper.
However, I have steadfastly refused to discuss publicly the contents of my paper until it passes through the procedures set up by my caucus and until all 72 of my Liberal colleagues who have not yet even seen the paper have the chance to read it. However, the reporters who have possession of my paper are under no such self-imposed restrictions. Even though the media is not prepared to print my own words unedited so that Canadians can draw their own conclusions, surely the journalists are prepared to provide Canadians with a copy of my paper if they call and ask. I will now provide the minister and Canadians with the names and telephone numbers of the journalists who have personally told me that they have a copy of my paper. If they send it to you, you can read it yourself and make up your own minds. While you are

talking to them, ask them the name of the person or persons who gave them the paper.
The names and telephone numbers are: Iain Hunter, The Ottawa Citizen, 613-232-4885; Paul Watson, Toronto Star, 416-869-4424; and Cecily Ross, Maclean's magazine, 416-596-6061.
Please, my fellow Canadians, never assume that what is reported is accurate. Find out the true facts for yourselves. You now know how. It is up to you.

speakeroldname: Mr. Jack Shields (Parliamentary Secretary to Minister of Employment and Immigration):
speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Employment and Immigration
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, my hon. friend for Scarborough West had asked a question on October 31 and is on the late show because of that question.
He did address something entirely different. I would like to say that I empathize with him. I know how unfortunate it can be when you are misquoted or remarks that you make are taken out of context. They then take on a life of their own.
I have worked in committee with my friend for Scarborough West. I have found him to be the type of individual I would be proud to serve on any committee
Adjournment Debate
with, particularly on the employment and immigration standing committee. I find that he has real empathy for people and a real empathy for the kinds of problems that we face with our immigration policy. He gives very constructive ideas and criticism where is it warranted and praise where that is also warranted.
I just want to say that I am sure with his remarks tonight we now can put that little rumour, the police cap, to bed. I want to assure my hon. friend that we will take this completely as he stated in the House. It is something that all of us understand.
We all at times do get into problems like this. We want him to know we empathize. It will blow over and we certainly will not hold him accountable for what the press has said.
